description:
Discovered while resolving JMAP-1j9k.12 (calendars-client got the if_in_state arg in line with canonical mail-client). Confirmed via grep that the following extension-client siblings do NOT expose if_in_state on any /set method:

- jmap-chat-client (Space/set, Message/set, Membership/set, ...)
- jmap-tasks-client (Task/set, TaskList/set)
- jmap-contacts-client (ContactCard/set, AddressBook/set)
- jmap-filenode-client (FileNode/set)
- jmap-sharing-client (Principal/set if any, ResourceShareGroup/set)

Canonical (jmap-mail-client) exposes if_in_state on:
- email_set (email.rs:104-117)
- email_import (email.rs:253-ish)
- email_submission_set (submission.rs:160-189)

Per workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' propagation rule, this is a cookie-cutter divergence: the canonical has the spec primitive, the siblings don't. RFC 8620 §5.3 if_in_state is the standard optimistic-concurrency guard; without it callers cannot atomically guard /set against concurrent modification.

Children (one per sibling):
.1 jmap-chat-client — sweep all *_set methods
.2 jmap-tasks-client — sweep task_set, task_list_set
.3 jmap-contacts-client — sweep contact_card_set, address_book_set
.4 jmap-filenode-client — sweep filenode_set
.5 jmap-sharing-client — sweep all *_set methods if applicable

Pattern (mirror canonical): trailing positional Option<&State> arg, wire shape:
    if let Some(s) = if_in_state { args["ifInState"] = s.as_ref().into(); }

Acceptance:
- Every *_set method in scope gains if_in_state: Option<&State>
- All existing call sites pass None for backward equivalence
- Each sibling's smoke tests retain green
- Workspace-level: cargo test --workspace + cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings green
- Out of scope: extending if_in_state to /import and /submission_set in non-mail crates (they don't have those methods)
title: Sweep: add RFC 8620 §5.3 if_in_state arg to /set methods across extension-client siblings
